title: SLA-driven boot hydration and KV seeder
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an SLA-aware boot hydration subsystem for Dedicated fleets that coordinates model weight streaming, staged kernel residency, and KV cache seeding. The goal is to guarantee per-tenant throughput SLOs during scale-up and placement events while minimizing wasteful full-weight residency and lowering cold-start tail latency for both synchronous and bursting traffic patterns.
background: Dedicated customers require predictable throughput guarantees (tokens/sec and P90 latency) even when scaled horizontally or when tenants experience sudden ramp-ups. Existing warm-pool heuristics prefetch whole weights or KV snapshots statically, which either wastes memory/IO or fails to reduce tail latency for multi-tenant bursty workloads. We need a coordinated approach that uses SLA metadata, lightweight probes, and staged hydration to hit guaranteed throughput targets with minimal resource overhead.
goals: 1) Meet tenant-level throughput SLAs during on-ramp events with >=95% success. 2) Reduce cold-start P95 latency by at least 40% for common model families. 3) Limit additional memory/io overhead to <10% of steady-state dedicated capacity. 4) Provide operators visibility into boot/hydration decisions and per-tenant admission outcomes.
technical_design:
Overview: introduce a Boot Hydrator service in the control plane that receives placement and autoscaling triggers. The Hydrator coordinates three cooperating mechanisms: (A) Staged weight hydration where weights are streamed in size-prioritized slices and earliest layers/kernels required for initial tokens are prioritized; (B) KV seeding which replays a short warm probe sequence to populate the per-tenant KV cache with high-value prefixes; (C) SLA-aware admission which reserves micro-slices of GPU memory and IO bandwidth based on tenant SLA tier and expected ramp delta.

Hydrator flow: on placement reserve -> estimate ramp profile using historical traffic and current autoscale intent -> allocate hydration budget (IO bandwidth, memory residency fraction) -> start parallel weight-slice stream prioritized by execution hotpath -> publish progress to fleet controller -> once minimal hydration milestone reached (kernel residency + KV probe success) mark instance as ready for low-latency traffic; continue background hydration to full residency.

Key algorithms: progressive layer-first streaming, KV probe selection using top-k ngram frequency from recent traffic, and admission control based on token-per-second budget. The Hydrator exposes a gRPC status API for Console and autoscaler to query readiness and expected ramp capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Automated experiment shows >=95% of simulated tenant on-ramps meet configured throughput targets within configured SLA window.
End-to-end test shows >=40% reduction in P95 cold-start latency for our canonical LLaMA-family workload compared to baseline warm-pool behavior.
Operator dashboard surfaces per-boot hydration timeline, IO/memory budget consumed, and admission decisions.
Hydrator respects per-tenant quotas and does not allow background hydration to breach reserved isolation limits.
New gRPC readiness endpoint returns consistent readiness states and estimated throughput capacity.
Security review sign-off obtained for control-plane hydration APIs and IAM scoping.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature flags and staging-only rollout for a single dedicated cluster. 2) Run synthetic tenant ramp tests at low traffic (10% of target). 3) Enable KV probe seeding for non-critical tenants and collect telemetry for two weeks. 4) Gradually enable admission-based hydration for P1 customers, monitor error budget. 5) Full rollout across Dedicated fleets after 4 weeks of stable metrics and SOC sign-off.
test_plan: Unit tests for streaming prioritization and slice reassembly
Integration test: full Hydrator + runtime in staging cluster with synthetic L7 traffic generator
Chaos test: simulated IO throttling and eviction during hydration to validate graceful degradation
Load test: tenant ramp scenarios (linear ramp, spike, sawtooth) to validate SLA hit rate
Security test: IAM and gRPC auth/authorization verification
risks: Underestimated IO contention could delay hydration causing SLA misses; mitigated by conservative initial budgets and adaptive backoff.
KV probe selection may not generalize to uncommon tenant prompts — we will keep fallback cold-fill paths and allow tenant-supplied probes.
Incorrect admission policies could starve other tenants; enforce strict global caps and monitor rejections.
Complexity in staged streaming increases failure modes during upgrades — include feature flag rollback and blue/green gating.
notes: We should coordinate with infra team to expose an IO-burst token bucket at the node level (ENG-272000 dependency).
Prototype observations: prioritizing attention layers reduced first-token latency by 18% in early tests.
Consider adding tenant-configurable probes (opt-in) for regulated customers to control what prefixes are seeded.
